events.body:
## Outcome

Communities can adopt ForkMesh while continuing to work on major centralized and self-hosted forges, with changes flowing safely in both directions.

## Scope

- Certify one major centralized provider and one self-hosted forge first, then add adapters behind a common provider contract.
- Synchronize refs, issues, pull requests, comments, reviews, labels, releases, identities, edits, and deletions with loop prevention.
- Expose mapping, lag, retries, conflicts, source-of-truth rules, and pause/resume controls.

## Acceptance criteria

- Repeated bidirectional sync is idempotent and never duplicates or silently overwrites records.
- Provider fixtures cover edits, deletion, force updates, rate limits, outages, and identity ambiguity.
- Sync lag meets the published SLO and every unresolved conflict is visible and recoverable.
- Linked automated evidence covers supported platforms, failure paths, rollback/recovery, documentation, and telemetry before closure.

## Delivery and dependencies

- Portfolio tier: **P0 release gate**
- Milestone: **Collaboration public beta**
- Numeric priority: **17 of 44** (1 is highest)
- Depends on: #477, #481, #483, #484
- Assignee: unassigned until an accountable owner accepts the epic; fund independently releasable child issues rather than this umbrella epic.

## Progress baseline

**20% as of 2026-07-22.** Git remotes can be mirrored and refreshed, but complete bidirectional collaboration adapters and conflict policy are not yet delivered. Progress may not exceed 85% without end-to-end validation or 95% without security, documentation, telemetry, and rollout evidence.

## Verification and measures

Primary measures: Sync lag, convergence rate, conflict rate, retry success, and retained external workflows. Closure requires linked test runs, operational evidence, and current user-facing documentation.
events.title: Build continuous two-way forge synchronization
